title: How did you all that awesome level design?
author: memphiz_
selftext:
I saw recently lot of cool projects and I think always “how did you do that?”  
I have a lot of assets from marketplace which I want to use and I want to use some LLMs to create some nice levels.  
I tried a lot using Codex (only sol at the moment to spare usage) and blender mcp or threejs direct but the wold looks always odd, it look even worse as I did it 😂

Do you have any tricks, guides, project where I can collect information how to utilize my agent better?

In the end I want to create a flat world with river, vegetation, houses(with indoor layout), city and villages. I know that I will not have this with one prompt. But even the pipeline/workflow for House, City or Vegetation/Rivers I feel I miss so much pieces of the puzzle 😩

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body: It does better with a reference. If you just say cook it with no context it goes potato. In normal level building. It's draw on paper then block it out then change to meshes then final detail sweep. I do the old game dev way with using the ai to build at 10x speed.

replies.author: memphiz_
replies.body: Ah good point, let me try this. Also for your assets did you maintain some kind of asset tagging meta file that the ai understand which assets you have?

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body: While I haven't built a finished level, I'm using fable to pull real-world data from AWS for terrain level information, then I "reach" it the trees / foliage. From there I had to do a lot of work showing it buildings and the modular kit I bought so it figured out how to rig them ... It's been a journey but finally sm somewhere I can use as an MVP.

comments.author: That1guy4226
comments.body: What engine did you wanna use? Godot unity or unreal? Or something else?

replies.author: memphiz_
replies.body: Currently I’m happy with threejs as rendering tool and no engine at all, what to have good old browser games back 😂

replies.author: That1guy4226
replies.body: Fair. I have been thinking about an old game from new grounds that I wanna try to remake. Specifically the Boxhead Zombie games

replies.author: AvonMexicola
replies.body: Use references, or let them make a reference using gpt image or something. Then let them rate how close they got to the reference and iterate. play.staragent.site I let Astra make this in JS.
